doc.title: Harold Danko interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 28, 2021

title: Lyrics of standards versus poetic rock; the Miles record
summary: He says standard lyrics meant little to him compared with Dylan and the Beatles; they discuss the Milestones LP and its blues and Red Garland track.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Those kind of things were poetic to me.
The words sort of came from a previous generation. It probably was a good thing that at age 12 you didn’t know about getting a kick from champagne I suppose.
I guess so, yeah, yeah I didn’t know about that yet.
But I think it’s so terrific that the Miles LP you mentioned, you know it starts out so ear- catching, like [scats]. How can that not grab you?
Yeah. Especially on a big stereo you know. It was just amazing. And then there’s so many, like bop, you know like on the other side, “Dr. Jekyll” you know stuff that’s really

— like I think there’s three things that are blues on the record. And then there’s that Red Garland thing “Billy Boy” which is kind of doing Ahmad Jamal but it’s with Philly Joe Jones so you know that’s some thrilling stuff you know.
